newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish deficit to end 1997 at 3.2 percent - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Spanish deficit to end 1997 at 3.2 percent - IMF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund forecasts Spanish public deficit at the end of 1997 at 3.2 percent, exceeding the three percent Maastricht criterion.
But the IMF also expects the ratio to decline toward 1.5 percent in 2000.
Spanish financial daily Expansion reported on Monday that the IMF latest report on Spain reiterated 1997 growth should be at around 2.8 percent.

Spanish gross domestic product should rise three and 3.5 percent before 2001 if the government undertakes liberalisation measures. If not, average growth would be around 2.5 percent, Expansion reported the IMF as saying.
Public debt is expected to fall to around 68.6 percent this year from 69.2 percent in 1996.
Spain CPI is expected to average in 1997 a 2.8 percent.
